question.problem:
$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+{e}^{y}}{e}, & \,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

The joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{3e+1}{6e},\,\text{E}[Y]=\frac{3}{2e},\,\text{SD}[X]≈0.2821,\,\text{SD}[Y]≈0.2870,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}xy\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\cdot (\frac{2x+{e}^{y}}{e})\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{e}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{2}y+xy{e}^{y})\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{e}{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}y+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}y{e}^{y}]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{e}{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{2}{3}y+\frac{1}{2}y{e}^{y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{e}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}y{e}^{y}-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{y}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{e}(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{e}{2}-\frac{e}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{6e}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{5}{6e}-(\frac{3e+1}{6e})(\frac{3}{2e}) \\  & =\frac{e-3}{12{e}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{(\frac{e-3}{12{e}^{2}})}{(0.2821)\cdot (0.2870)} \\  & ≈-0.04,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
